business_question: Does Amazon's revenue concentration in the European Union create hidden exposure to EUR/USD foreign exchange risk?
description: Amazon's International segment — primarily European operations across Germany, UK, France, Italy, Spain, Netherlands, Poland, and Sweden — generated approximately $131bn in 2023, representing roughly 25% of total net sales. This revenue is earned in EUR, GBP, and other European currencies but reported in USD. When USD strengthens relative to EUR (as it did materially in 2022), Amazon's International segment revenue translates to fewer dollars, directly reducing reported net sales and operating income. An investor holding Amazon who focuses on AWS growth and US retail may not recognise the substantial EUR/USD exposure embedded in the International segment. Note: 'europe' node is distinct from 'european-union' (regulatory jurisdiction) — Amazon's revenue geography includes UK (post-Brexit) and other non-EU European markets.
